title: Using Participle Adjectives to Describe a Memory

sections.title: Making a memory vivid with one word
sections.content: Participle adjectives are especially useful for describing memories, because a memory is often defined by what happened in it. Two more words help: *benyomás* ("impression") in the set phrase *mély benyomást tesz rám* ("makes a deep impression on me"), and *megérint* ("to touch, to move emotionally") — itself a verb that becomes the participle *megérintett* ("touched, moved") when you want to describe a reaction as an adjective.

items.spanish: Ez a találkozás mély benyomást tett rám.
items.english: This encounter made a deep impression on me.

items.spanish: Egy megérintett, csendes hallgatóság ült a teremben.
items.english: A moved, silent audience sat in the room.

sections.content: *mély benyomást tesz rám* behaves like a fixed phrase: *mély* ("deep") describes *benyomás* ("impression"), *tesz* ("makes") is the verb, and *rám* ("on me") carries the person affected — change only *rám* (*rád*, *rá*, *ránk*...) to say who was impressed, and leave the rest of the phrase alone.
